{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows sustained negative sentiment (e.g., multiple -0.25 or 0.00 values), as models tend to overestimate prices in such periods.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility after a sharp price spike; models often overshoot post-spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above or below recent 5-day average, adjust toward it, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.",
    "Increase downward bias when sentiment history includes 0.00 or 0.33 values in recent days, indicating market cooling or uncertainty.",
    "Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5 days of 30d forecast) when sentiment is neutral or positive — models tend to overestimate prices in such windows.",
    "When sentiment history includes 0.50 or higher, model forecasts should be slightly conservative — avoid upward momentum unless supported by strong recent price action.",
    "If true outcome deviates significantly from forecast in the first 5 days of the 30d window, adjust future forecasts to reflect a more gradual trend, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative."
  ]
}
